La façon la meilleure et la plus sûre de savoir si vous êtes censé être avec votre partenaire pour le reste de votre vie est la suivante : est-ce que je fais confiance à cette personne et puis-je lui faire confiance ? Emerging from the shambles of former
response:
The five members of indie rock darlings Grand Duchy, Dawes, recently relocated to Northern California—and they're ready to put all those hours to work in their new 1,600-square-foot post.
The band's self-titled debut is an easy go with its "modern" (read: updated classic-rock) sound, a well-mixed yet accessible mix of 12 songs with good beats and a more than passable lead vocalist in Taylor Goldsworthy. Dawes, however, isn't just your typical old school rock band with some modern credibility—the band's rootsy rock with pop production touches is part of its charm. Goldsworthy is good at writing pop songs, as he showed during his time with the very pop Grand Duchy, but the best things here are his raw sing-song vocals that are either soaring and angelic, or raspy and heartfelt. The rest of the band's hard work pays off as well.

The Pinwheels and Ribbon Cowl is a simple piece that lets you knit one pinwheel and one ribbon at a time; You knit a few pins straight, and then knit a few pins backwards to get the ribs. To create the cowl's seamless, tensioned tubular shape without a joining seam, you join a pinwheel row to a ribbon row. It is completely "natural" in every way, and a pleasure to knit. You can make three or four rows of ribbon for a little teepee, or a longer, more-streamlined "drape" (a pinwheel row makes the fabric wider, while a ribbon row keeps it from folding; this is why you want fewer ribbon rows). When I was first developing this pattern, I did a bunch of swatches just for fun, and the result is some pretty pinwheel and ribbon "curtains", so that's how it was.
